tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

# Writing the skills

The curator directs this restoration and reads every skill with human eyes. The writer edits a skill, a part is a file under its `references/`, and the record is the project's memory under `explorations/`. The register is Simplified Technical English (ASD-STE100), about halfway. Each principle gives its reason, then a text he marked and the text he accepted.

## 1. Define a term before you use it, and use plain words everywhere else

A reader new to the repository has only the skill, its brief and its training. A word with a meaning that the record gave it (a defect's "home", a "stop" that does not stop, "corpus") tells it nothing or the wrong thing. Where its training holds a near thing, name it ("as LLVM's lit does"): one clause corrects an assumption where a paragraph would not.
- Marked: "In every report, give each defect's home, ..."
- Accepted: "In your report, list each defect that you found, with the test or ledger row that records it."

## 2. Put the concepts first, as a dictionary, then the procedures in the order that the work meets them

A chain of do's and don'ts cannot be held in mind; a concept named once (an area, building, exploring, a point to report) makes each procedure short and tells the reader when to switch. A glossary entry is the term, then a noun phrase with no article. A comment marks a problem area: fix it at its paragraph or section, with the whole skill in mind.
- Marked: "- The base is the commit that your work starts from."
- Accepted: "**base**" / ": Commit that your work starts from."

## 3. Every sentence tells the reader what to do or a fact it needs to do it; cut the rest

Every agent pays for every token, and a sentence that changes nothing hides the ones that do: a slogan (a decision's title copied from the record), a step the agent takes anyway, a rule it cannot act on, a rule against a failure that never happened, a rule its system prompt gives, a back reference, a provenance word.
- Marked: "1. Read your brief. 2. Load the parts below that your task touches. [...] 4. Do the work."
- Accepted: "Load the parts below that your task touches before you run the query of the record that your brief gives. The parts give the words [...]"

## 4. State a rule for exactly the cases where it holds, and bound it to the agent's brief and its own work

A wider rule sends the agent to do what cannot be done: a test for a specification edit, a search through other agents' transcripts, a question to the curator. An absolute ("never wipe the caches") is wrong in the cases it did not name. Authority reaches an agent through its brief alone, and what a role or a workflow does belongs there, not in the skill.
- Marked: "Before you build or run something, look for its result on record. If the record or another agent's transcript holds the result [...], cite that result"
- Accepted: "Reuse each result of a build, a suite, a stage of the gate or a test that your brief cites or that your own work ran. Cite it."

Misapplied: cutting the default for a silent brief ("If it says nothing, commit your own files as you go") leaves the agent with no action. A cut never removes a default.

## 5. Say what to do, in the positive, one instruction per sentence, the condition first; add a reason only where it helps judge a case the rule does not name

A prohibition hides the mechanism it protects ("Do not ask the curator anything" hid how a question reaches him), and a compressed rule loses its purpose. A sentence that carries a list, a quoted title and a pointer cannot be held in mind; three short ones can.
- Marked: "Change one variable per step."
- Accepted: "When you probe or debug, change one thing at a time, so that each result has one cause."

## 6. State a fact once, where the reader builds on it, and never in more words than the text you replace

The curator reads for duplication at every scale: a word written twice, a fact said twice, a paragraph where a sentence does. A longer rewrite is a regression, however clear.
- Marked: "Do not pipe `ant` through `tail`: `tail` prints only after the command ends, and only its last lines. If the Bash tool's time limit stops the run first, you see nothing [...]"
- Accepted: "Do not pipe `ant` through `tail`: if the Bash tool's time limit stops the command, it shows nothing."

Misapplied: a word repeated for two things (the `walk` command walks the tree) is not duplication; the rule is one word for one thing, and a pronoun for the second mention of the same thing.

## 7. Put knowledge in the part loaded when it is needed; name a note only with a trigger and a narrow read

A mention of a file does not make an agent open it at the right moment, and a large note read whole costs more than the task. So the part holds what daily work needs, and a note it names comes with when to open it and the query that prints the slice. What only the coordinating session needs stays out of a skill every worker loads.
- Marked: "`explorations/modernization-plan.md` gives the versions and the classfile level."
- Accepted: "Before you change the version of a tool, read its step in the modernization plan. [...] It prints 4 to 6 KB: `facts-extract.sh 'doc:explorations/modernization-plan.md#The ladder@TOOL'`."

## P45: fidelity and comprehensibility are separate checks

On October 22 the curator supplied a screenshot and copied text of a proposed P-45 revision from the positions audit. The artifact URL could not be retrieved; this review concerns the supplied example, not the entire list. The screenshot distinguishes deletions from retained text; the copied text alone mixes both. The original ruling and its provenance have not been re-audited here.

**Finding:** removing historical material improves the entry but does not by itself make the remaining decision understandable. The difficulty is visible in the formulation, not necessarily a lack of Fortress knowledge on the reader's part.

- It mixes requirements with statements of implementation behaviour. “The checker runs” and “walk and the checker accept the same pairs” read as established facts, while “Still to build” points to remaining disagreements. State clearly whether agreement is a requirement or an achieved result.
- “No parameter pair required to exclude”, “refused families” and “reads otherwise” conceal important meaning in compressed technical wording. Name the objects and the operation precisely.
- “The paper's three overloading rules” neither identifies the paper precisely nor states enough of the decision to orient the reader. A reference may supply detail; it should not replace the explanation of what was decided.
- “No model line changes” compresses a consequential constraint into project shorthand. Identify the microGPT model program and state the exact restriction established by the ruling.
- A tracked diff makes historical and current wording compete for attention. Show the clean proposed entry first, with the diff available underneath.

### Proposed form, subject to checking the ruling

Lead with the decision. Follow with its essential scope, reason and exact technical conditions. Distinguish any remaining implementation work and point to its proper record. Preserve conditions that limit the decision; do not simplify away those conditions merely to improve fluency.

An illustrative opening is:

> **P-45 — Use the 2011 overloading model in the specification and both execution paths.** Allow overloads whose static parameters differ. The compiler's checker and the interpreter must apply the same rules when deciding which overload declarations are permitted.

This is a presentation example, **not a verified replacement for P45**. It must be checked against the curator's actual ruling before adoption, and it does not replace the technical requirements omitted from this short opening. In the final entry, identify the 2011 source precisely. Do not turn an implementation default or a writer's inference into the curator's decision.

### Two checks in the existing rewrite process

1. **Fidelity:** compare the proposed entry with the recorded ruling and its qualifications. Distinguish the curator's words from the coordinator's interpretation, an implementation choice and a fact about the current tree. Keep the provenance in history.
2. **Comprehensibility:** give a cold reader the clean entry and its declared prerequisite context, without the original discussion. Ask it to paraphrase what the curator decided, where it applies, what it requires, and what remains unfinished. Compare that paraphrase with the source-backed meaning. If the reader has to reconstruct the original discussion to resolve the wording, revise the entry.

The acceptance question is:

> Can a reader distinguish what Pavol decided, what the implementation currently does, and what remains unfinished?

A citation establishes where a statement came from; it does not establish that the statement communicates its meaning. This check does not require a type-theory lesson inside every position. It requires enough context to identify the decision before following pointers for technical detail.

This is a proposed improvement to positions writing, distinct from Revival's admission rule. A ruling remains part of POSITIONS even when a worker would already agree with it by default. No POSITIONS entry, skill or audit proposal was edited here.

## For Fable: rewrite positions before consolidating Revival

**Current priority, requested by the curator on October 22:** finish the faithful, readable rewriting of POSITIONS before consolidating the skill's Revival part. This section is the starting brief for that work; the rest of this report supplies background. It does not authorize changing a ruling or treating a proposed wording as an approved decision.

### Reader and register

Assume the reader knows the relevant language concepts, or can reach their definitions through the normal skill references, but does not remember the conversation that produced the decision. A position must communicate the ruling without requiring that conversation.

Apply the project's existing **ASD-STE100-inspired register (“halfway”)** to these entries, not only to skills. Read:

- `explorations/coordinator/skill-writer-brief.md`, section 1, for the writing guidance.
- `explorations/reviews/skills-writing-principles.md`, for the worked examples and principles.
- `.claude/skills/coordinator/references/record.md`, for entry ownership, scope, history and the record-writing procedure.

These are writing references, not a request to adopt unrelated skill-writer duties. Use familiar verbs, explicit subjects and antecedents, consistent technical terms, and one main point per sentence. Put the condition before the action when that makes the rule easier to follow. Separate a decision from its reason and implementation status. Short sentences must preserve qualifications; do not meet a word target by replacing precise meaning with shorthand.

The curator suspects that older entries predate this register and have not received a comparable prose pass. That chronology has not been established entry by entry. The observed wording defects justify the clarity pass regardless of their age. This is an adaptation of ASD-STE100 guidance, not a claim of formal compliance.

### What the supplied examples show

The P45, P50 and P51 reviews are based on the curator's pasted text and screenshots of proposed edits, not a fresh verification of the original rulings.

**P45 needs structural clarification.** Separate what the curator requires from claims about achieved behaviour. Lead with the decision; retain exact technical restrictions; put detailed implementation gaps in their existing record homes, with a concise pointer where needed. The illustrative opening in the preceding P45 section remains provisional.

**P50 and P51 need a smaller clarity pass.** Each already centres on a recognizable rule. Removing the historical material is useful; do not require a wholesale rewrite merely because the reader needs language knowledge.

For P50:

- Replace the grammatical compression “its exits' with values” with wording that explicitly identifies the values supplied by exits.
- “P-51 is the other half of item 48” describes the old discussion's organization. State the substantive relationship if it helps the reader; otherwise leave that association in history.
- Expected-type propagation into the label body and its exits is the central decision. Keep its scope intact. Verify any proposed restatement against the ruling rather than inferring further type-theoretical claims from it.

For P51:

- “When the checker's attempts at a call keep none” should identify exactly what the initial check failed to find. “If the initial check finds no applicable overload” is a possible wording **only if it matches the recorded trigger**.
- Distinguish the outer call from the inner call used as its argument. Repeated uses of “call” should not force the reader to infer which one is meant.
- Preserve the boundary “any inferred static argument, not only a result-only type parameter”. This affects which cases the decision covers.
- Replace “it makes the inference rules one rule everywhere” with the particular consistency the ruling sought. Do not widen the decision or invent a stronger rationale.
- The probe's measurement belongs in its report. A short implementation-status statement can remain if it accurately reports the relevant completion; it must not imply that every related gap is closed.

### A bounded rewrite and check

For each entry already under review:

1. Recover the ruling and its qualifications from the provenance gathered by the current audit. Distinguish the curator's decision from a coordinator default, a worker choice and an implementation fact.
2. Write the clean proposed entry in the register above. Preserve the permanent identifier. Keep decision, scope and essential reason together. Retain technical conditions that affect what is allowed.
3. Check fidelity against the source, including whether the rewrite makes the claim stronger or broader. Keep historical wording and provenance in the established history mechanism.
4. Check comprehension with the normal prerequisite context but without the original discussion. Ask the reader to restate the decision, its trigger and limits, and any unfinished work.
5. Classify a failure before fixing it: missing language concept, unclear wording, or uncertain fidelity. Supply or link a definition for the first; rewrite the second; return to the evidence or curator for the third.
6. Present the clean proposal first and its diff underneath for the curator's review. Apply approved edits through the existing record tooling and preserve their history.

This refines the existing fidelity and cold-reader checks; it does not require a new large audit or a separate agent for every entry. Focus review effort on changed or ambiguous decisions.

**Acceptance question:** can a reader with the normal language prerequisites explain what Pavol decided and where it applies, without reconstructing the original conversation?

Do not inflate Revival to supply all those prerequisites. Ordinary language concepts belong in the core or appropriate area reference. Revival retains its narrower role of correcting mistaken assumptions about revived Fortress. Nor should a ruling be removed from POSITIONS merely because it matches a worker's default belief: the per-entry necessity test for Revival is not a deletion rule for the curator's decisions.

No POSITIONS entries or skill files were changed by this report update.

## For Claude: assess all FACTS, rewrite only failing entries

# The review's findings, and the run that corrects them

## Summary

The review's findings are readings of the team's sources, not traces of the curator's words. In 18 entries it found a reason from the wrong layer or date, a missing ground from the language's texts, a false statement, a sentence not his, or a word of his still owed. Each right reading rests on dated lines of the specification, the papers, the library, the code or git; his words give the frame and show what he decided. All nine decisions stand. The mining workflow asks whose words an entry records: its scouts check only what an entry states, and its writer keys a change to his words. The clarity workflow's steps fit, with each finding's ground as the source: an Opus writer stream, the cold read, the checker, the judge, the trap test and his read of a first chunk. Three briefs and a README need short additions, marked below. The process lacks a findings input, a check of length and registe

## 0. Sources

Paths start at `explorations/`. F is `reviews/foundations/`; J is `F/judgement.md`; S is `F/evidence/salvage-findings.md`; M is `coordinator/positions-audit/full/evidence/briefs/`; C is `coordinator/tools/record-clarity/`; A is `coordinator/postmortem-2026-10-28/account.md`.

## 1. The findings

**How the review reached them.**

- On 10-24, Opus mapped the decisions against the designers' word; a Fable judge ruled (`reviews/phase3-exit/README.md`, layers 1, 2).
- On 10-26, on his frame of three layers (the language, the team's build on the JVM, Java interoperability; 05:25:27 UTC), workers gathered evidence with no verdicts: a Sonnet archaeology of the bound, an Opus probe of it compiled, an Opus map of the nine tenets' grounds by layer "checked at the source", and an Opus sweep of the revival's changes against the prelude, each prelude line dated by its first commit (`F/tenets-evidence.md`, header; `F/prelude-lens.md`, section 0; `F/bound-archaeology.md`, section 0).
- The map took his words from the audit's scout reports of 10-22 and the transcripts, as one input beside the texts (`F/tenets-evidence.md`, "Abbreviations").
- A Fable judge checked the key lines at source, and ruled each tenet (J, header, section 2). The trap test found where old texts mislead. Climb batch 22c's planner found the abstract-member ground false (`F/rewrite-results.md`). A Sonnet worker listed the findings per entry, each with its ground (S).

**The kinds.** All nine decisions hold. The faults are in the entries' reasons and statements (J, section 1, items 1 and 2).

1. **A reason from the wrong layer or with the wrong date.** The team's later word (P-26) counts 2009 prelude code as later than texts of 2010 to 2012. The flat number types (P-43) call the prelude "the team's last record of the Fortress way". One library (P-37) takes prelude designs with no rule. The integer power (P-153) calls compiled-path code the later word; list order (P-154) cites a draft of unknown date. The specification's revision (P-7) mixes two kinds of "later work in the compiler". The self-type idiom (P-146) gives a reason that misled a reader.
   - Right reading: "later" is a date among the language's texts. The team's code is its word on the language only where it wrote the rule on purpose, or where its checker enforced a rule that the text leaves silent or ambiguous. A stub or a JVM accommodation does not bind (J, section 3).
   - Evidence: `6896886fb` (2009-08-31) against the Working Draft's last edit (2010-12); Naden, 2012-08-31 (`justificationOfRTR.tex:626-630`); "Hopefully temporary hack" (`WellKnownNames.java:113-116`); the root snapshot `5a68404fd` (S; J, tenets 2, 3).
2. **A missing ground from the language.** Unboxed doubles (P-17), the bound `Any` (P-42 c), the flat number types (P-43 b), the natives' form (P-58 a), one library (P-37 a).
   - Right reading: the decision rests on the language's own text, or on the library's practice where the language is silent.
   - Evidence: `objects.tex:38`, `binary.tex:80`; `ParkPOPL2019.txt:418-419` and the Working Draft's `trait-parameters.tex:53-54`; the exclusion rule's four texts and `types-vals-vars.tex:502`; `future.tex:675`, no foreign-function interface; for P-37, his goal of 10-26 04:47:50 (S).
3. **A false or stale statement.** The bound `Any` (P-42 a, b, d): "functions", a switch-over that "ends the departure", the arrays' example. One library (P-37 c, d): its premise, three files. The phase order (P-33): "whole library". Walk runs the checker (P-12): its size. The `double[]` store (P-84): stamping alone gives no `double[]` field. Abstract members (P-158 a, b): the export rule and the date.
   - Evidence: `Shell.java:372`, F-289; `types-vals-vars.tex:136` against `types.tick:232-238`; `FortressLibrary.fsi:759`; F-34, F-53, F-290; `StaticChecker.java:228-229`; `CompilerSystem` and its 27 tests; `array-design.md`, section 2; `source-code.tex:372-385`, `edb516dba` (2009-03-10) (S).
4. **A sentence not his.** The team's later word (P-26 b), walk's coercions (P-59), part of P-43 a. Evidence: commits and his dated words (S).
5. **His word still owed.** The natives' form (P-58 b), symbolic operators (P-155), his lean of 09-20 on arrays (P-85). No text follows from a source.

**Outside the list.** S covers only the foundations reports (its header). The exit judgement ruled text corrections of the same kinds for float rounding (P-68), the team demos (P-79), the self-type idiom (P-146), existential reduction (P-152), list order (P-154), symbolic operators (P-155) and the `Index` bound (P-156) (`reviews/phase3-exit/judgement.md`, section 3.2; review queue, items 285 to 290).

## 2. How the mining workflow differs

- Its question is provenance: "the curator's decision, faithfully recorded, or an agent's summary or default" (`coordinator/positions-audit/README.md`).
- The scout finds "what the curator said, what he was asked", and checks the tree "Only where the entry states a reason, a premise, a number or a fact about the tree" (M`scout.md`). It neither seeks a missing ground nor ranks grounds by layer or date.
- The judge classes each part by origin: his decision, a default, no source (M`judgement.md`).
- The writer keys a change to his words: rule 1 "checked against his words", rule 4 "reworded from his intent", rule 5 "No source of his" becomes a question, rule 12 "His later word" (M`writer.md`). Only rule 8, a premise "corrected from its source", acts on the team's sources. Rule 0, "Change as little as you can.", fits any correction.
- The takeaway check compares with "what the curator decided, as his messages show it" (M`takeaway.md`); `hischeck.py` checks his quotes.
- So the mining tool finds kind 4 and part of kind 3.

## 3. Which steps fit, and against what

- **Writer** (Opus stream, C`writer.md`). Fits, with rule 0: it writes from each finding's ground, opened at source, and keeps the decision his. Two lines block it: "Keep the meaning." and step 3, a reason "only if the curator gave one or accepted it in the question".
- **Cold read** (C`coldread.md`). Fits as it is, against nothing: a reader with only the worker skill says what each entry asks.
- **Checker** (C`check.md`). Fits, against each finding's ground. For FACTS it already reads "the code or test it names"; for POSITIONS its sources are only the audit's evidence of his words. The decision itself is still checked against his words (C`entries.py`). Its check of the cold reader's answers replaces the takeaway check.
- **Judge** (C`judge.md`). Fits: apply or hold, the old text the default, a held entry's question to the review queue.
- **Quiz** (the trap test, `F/evidence/trap-test/`). Fits: it grades a reader's decisions at forks against a key from the judgement and his words. It quotes 7 of the 18 (P-26, P-27, P-33, P-37, P-42, P-43, P-146).
- **His read** of a first chunk, old beside new. Fits: only it checks tone, length, register and history in an entry (A, section 2, cause 4).

**What the process lacks.**

- An input for a review's findings: no stage reads one (`tool-fit.md`, section 2).
- A rule that lets a ground from the team's sources into an entry (C`writer.md`, step 3; M`writer.md`, rules 1 to 12).
- A check of length against the old entry, of register and of history (`tool-fit.md`, section 4). `record.py check` flags only entries over 600 characters.
- Quiz scenarios for 11 of the 18. J drafts a trap for six of them (section 7, "Trap:").
- An audit trace of abstract members (P-158): `entries.py` knows only the audit's chunks.

## 4. The run

**A writer's inputs for one entry**, beyond what C`writer.md` names:

- The entry, its history, and the audit's evidence of his words, of 10-22 (`entries.py N`).
- Its block of S, in `findings.md` in the chunk's folder, cut by script to the chunk's entries.
- Each ground the block names, opened at source; the review passage it cites, for content only.
- Not the rejected texts of 10-26, their run brief, or J's section 7 as a target.

**Brief changes**, for his yes, made by the skill writer on Opus:

- C`writer.md`, after "Keep the meaning.": "**Corrections.** If your folder holds `findings.md`, a review found faults in your entries, each with its ground. Correct each named sentence from its ground, opened at its source, and change nothing else (the audit writer's rule 0). A reason may rest on the team's texts, library or code that a finding cites; the curator's words show what he decided. Where a finding has no ground but a reviewer's reasoning, or needs his word, write a question, not text. An entry grows only by what a correction needs."
- C`writer.md`, step 3, end of its first sentence: "or a finding in `findings.md` gives it with its ground."
- C`check.md`, after the positions sources: "With `findings.md`, a corrected sentence's source is its finding's ground; open it. A change that its ground holds is no fidelity failure. A change that no finding names is one, and so are a changed decision, growth beyond the corrections, and a sentence that tells history."
- C`judge.md`, the folder's files: add "`findings.md`, whose grounds are sources".
- C`README.md`, "Running it": "To correct a review's findings, put them in each chunk's folder as `findings.md`."
- No change to the script, `coldread.md` or `fix.md`.

**Chunks**, by subject, each written by the tool's Opus writer stream (A, section 5, step 1):

- c1, alone first: P-7, P-26, P-27, P-37, P-43, P-146, P-153, P-154, P-158.
- c2: P-12, P-17, P-33, P-42, P-58, P-59, P-84, P-85, P-155.
- If the exit judgement's corrections join the scope, a retrieval worker adds their findings, and c3 takes P-68, P-79, P-152, P-156.

**The coordinator's steps.** Copy the findings; launch with arguments only. A worker applies `final.apply` on a copy and runs `record.py check --base`, a length table old against new, and `words-subset.py` on the strike-only entries (P-26 b, P-59, P-42 a). # Chunk c2: corrections from the findings

Only the sentences that a finding names change. Every other sentence is the text of POSITIONS at `5da8144e4`, word for word. Three findings need the curator's word and have no ground in the team's sources: P-58 (b), P-85 and P-155. Those entries keep their text, and each has a question.

## P-33

- P-33 **The work toward microGPT compiled follows the phases, in the order that the curator approved.** These phases are steps of the work, not the compiler's phases, and they are numbered 3 to 6, after two earlier ones. Phase 3: the compiled checker reports no error on the twelve apis and twelve components of the interpreter's library that the distance to the switch-over counts (the distance at zero; F-53 defines it and holds its value). The library's other components are not part of phase 3; F-290 counts their errors. Phase 4, the switch-over: first the natives, the library's `builtinPrimitive` bindings made to run on the compiled path, then the compiled path reads the interpreter's library and the compiler's prelude is deleted; phase 5, microGPT compiles: its static types, the array design and the code generator's open gaps; phase 6, microGPT runs fast. Code-generator work goes on beside that order, under either library (P-37). Row 320, an api implemented by a component of another name does not link, is part of the switch-over's design.

Meaning: one change, from the finding. The old text said that phase 3's checker "reports no error on the interpreter's whole library". The distance counts only twelve apis and their twelve components (F-53). The new text names them, and a new sentence says that the other components are outside phase 3.

Sources:
- The scope of the zero: F-53 ("its twelve apis and their twelve components").
- The other components: F-290 measures them outside the twelve. The curator agreed that the plan never meant them for phase 3: his "Of course" of 2026-10-26T04:47:50Z, to the coordinator's "the word 'whole' is wrong" (`conversations/02-phase3-exit-foundations.md`, section 4; the coordinator's sort of the findings, item 7). In the same message his goal is "the fuller Fortress library that the interpreter uses"; P-37 holds that goal, so this entry does not repeat it.
- "Phase 3:" and "Phase 4, the switch-over:" now open sentences, because a new sentence stands between them. Their words are unchanged.
- The other sentences: the text at `5da8144e4`.

# Concepts for chunk c2

Chunk c1's `concepts.md` already lists the switch-over, the distance to the switch-over, the compiler's prelude, the compiled checker, the Working Draft, the Types chapter of the team's 2012 restart and "row N". This chunk uses them too: P-33, P-42, P-58, P-59, P-84, P-85 and P-155. Only the concepts below are new.

- **native binding**: a library body that is exactly `builtinPrimitive("…")`, whose string names the Java code that runs it. Used by P-33, P-58. P-58 defines it; the `fortress-repo` core should name it in one line beside "one library", since phase 4 starts with it.
- **glue class**: a Java class of walk that a native binding names; it takes walk's boxed values. Used by P-58 (and F-32). Define in the `fortress-repo` area part on the interpreter.
- **static helper**: a static Java method in `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/nativeHelpers/`, over plain Java values, that the compiled path calls for a native. Used by P-58. Define in the area part on the code generator.
- **the class loader's stamping**: the compiled path's way of making a generic instance's class at its first use, by renaming the template's type parameters in its bytecode (`InstantiatingClassloader`). Used by P-84 (and F-18). The `fortress-repo` core's "The compiled run time" gives the mechanism; it should use the word "stamping" once, since the record uses it.
- **the array decisions A, B and D**: the open decisions of the compiled path's array design: A, how an `RR64` array made through the generic array traits gets a `double[]` store; B, where unboxed arithmetic happens; D, the sizes in the model's own types. Used by P-84, P-85. P-85 defines them; no skill needs them before the array work.
- **way A4**: the way for decision A in which the class loader stamps an `RR64` instance with a `double[]` field. Used by P-84 (and F-18). Defined in `reviews/array-design-ways.md`, section 3; P-84 glosses it, so no skill needs it.
- **the extends-`Object` setting**: the pre-desugaring switch that gives an unbounded type parameter the bound `Object`, on under `fortress compile` (`Shell.useCompilerLibraries()`) and off under walk and the distance stage. Used by P-42 (and F-289). Define in the `fortress-repo` area part on the compiler, where `compiler.md` now says that the switch-over ends it.
- **the overloading check and the export check**: two separate checks of the compiled checker. The overloading check tests that the overloads of one name are valid; the export check compares a component's declarations with its api's. Both skip the top-level symbolic operators today (row 584, row 782). Used by P-155. Define both in the area part on the checker, so that "the check" in a record entry can be told apart.
